notes:
0.9.70-beta 173 Paris
• LitArbi for Word: LitArbi's tab and citation pane inside Word, from Microsoft's add-in store — on the Mac, Windows, the web and the iPad, with every command of the old ribbon.
• One click switches from the old Word add-in: connect once, the old one goes to the Trash, add LitArbi for Word in the store.
• Word for Mac older than 16.70 keeps the ribbon add-in and LitArbi's own pane, as before.
• The connection stays on this Mac (127.0.0.1) and only your own programs may use it.
• Each brief remembers its matter: LitArbi for Word picks it again, or opens it in LitArbi with one click.
• Links that Travel: a citation opens its exhibit at the cited page on any Mac with the matter, in a Share Matter copy and on the iPad.
• Edit Exhibit finds a citation pasted without its bookmark.
• Date ranges on exhibits: “1 March – 5 April 2021”, in citations, lists and the chronology.
• Citation templates take *bold*, _italic_ and ++underline++.
• LitArbi for LibreOffice 1.1: Writer cites as Word does — your templates, links, Update Exhibits, the List of Exhibits as tables.
• Settings ▸ Storage: sign in with Microsoft 365 and keep your exhibit files in a SharePoint library — also without a server; synced folders work too.
• LitArbi for Word and LibreOffice in Portuguese (Portugal), as the app since 0.9.66.
• A Portugal matter stays Portuguese when you write the term your own way ("Doc. nº").
• Malay (Bahasa Malaysia): OCR on this Mac, and translation from and into Malay with the AI providers (DeepL has none).
• Malaysia (Ekshibit P1): citations, the Senarai Ekshibit and dates in Bahasa Malaysia, also in LitArbi for Word.
• DeepL now also translates into Dutch, Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Czech and Romanian.
• More dates read as dates: “12 maio 2009”, “1-5 April 2021”, and a month with its year (“May 2009”), now written in words.
